readerTitle: When should a rival's price set yours?
caseNote: 가상 사례 2개 (철물점, 동네 비스트로) + 가상 적용 (소프트웨어) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 경쟁사 가격은 고객이 나란히 비교할 수 있는 만큼만 내 가격을 정한다. 비교가 쉬우면 맞추고, 다르면 그 가격을 출발점으로 삼아 차이만큼 더하거나 뺀다.
misconception: 경쟁사보다 비싸면 무조건 손님을 잃는다. 그러니 경쟁사 가격에 맞추거나 더 낮추는 것이 가장 안전하다.

sources.text: 가격 전략의 표준 개념 (경쟁 기반 가격 책정, 소매업의 주요 비교 품목 관리)

factChecks.note: 비스트로: 체인 점심 $11, 비스트로 $14, 차이 $3. 수치는 모두 가상입니다. 소프트웨어: 경쟁사 사용자당 월 $10, 제안 가격 $14는 설명용 가정입니다.
소매업체가 고객이 가격을 잘 기억하는 소수 품목(known-value items)은 경쟁사에 맞추고 다른 품목에서 이익을 낸다는 내용은 업계에서 널리 쓰이는 관행으로 일반적으로 서술했습니다. 구체적 기업명이나 수치는 넣지 않았습니다.

cards.title: When should a rival's price set yours?
body: Two owners on the same street check their competitors' prices every Monday. One runs a hardware store. The other runs a small bistro.
They do the same homework. Only one of them should let the answer set the price.

image.label: Two shop owners peeking at rival price tags
image.brief: 한 거리의 두 가게. 왼쪽 철물점 주인은 쌍안경으로 맞은편 대형 매장의 드릴 가격표를, 오른쪽 비스트로 주인은 옆 체인 식당의 메뉴판을 보고 있음. 따뜻한 일러스트 스타일, 실제 브랜드 로고나 상표는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: The big chain just cut the price of your best-selling drill.
body: You run a hardware store. A popular cordless drill, the exact same model and brand, sells for $129 at your store. You pay $85 for it.
The big chain across town drops it to $109. Customers can check both prices on their phones in seconds. What do you do?

options.text: Match $109 on this drill, and leave your other prices alone
options.feedback: You earn $24 instead of $44 per drill, but you stop looking expensive on the one item people compare. Next card shows why that matters.

options.text: Keep $129 and point to your friendly service
options.feedback: Service matters, but this drill is identical everywhere. A $20 gap on a product people can compare in seconds makes your whole store look pricey.
You give up $10 per drill and still lose the side-by-side comparison by $10. You pay for a cut without getting its benefit.

cards.title: Same homework, different answers.
body: The hardware store matched. Its drill is the same box the chain sells, so customers compare price and almost nothing else.

The bistro owner saw a chain lunch spot nearby charging $11. Her lunch special is $14. She almost cut it, then noticed her regulars weren't comparing. Her soup is made that morning, the room is quiet, and she knows their names. There's no identical item to put side by side. She kept $14, and the room stayed full.

image.label: Identical drill boxes vs two very different lunch plates
image.brief: 화면을 반으로 나눔. 왼쪽: 똑같은 드릴 상자 두 개가 저울 위에 나란히 있고 가격표 $109 / $129. 오른쪽: 체인점 포장 샌드위치와 비스트로의 수프·빵 접시, 가격표 $11 / $14, 접시 모양이 확연히 다름. 로고 없음.

cards.title: Competitor-based pricing
body: **Competitor-based pricing** means setting your price by looking at what rivals charge for a similar offer. You can price at, below or above them.

The key word is *similar*. A rival's price matters exactly as much as customers use it to judge yours. The hardware store faced a direct comparison. The bistro didn't, so the chain's $11 was a reference point, not a rule.

cards.title: Ask one question: how easily can customers compare?
body: Before you react to a rival's price, place your offer on this scale.
list: **Same product, price easy to see:** stay close to the rival, or explain the gap clearly
**Similar product, a few real differences:** start from the rival's price, then add or subtract for each difference
**Different product or experience:** treat the rival's price as a rough anchor only
cards.callout: The closer to identical, the more the rival's price is your price.
cards.softwareNote: Software buyers line up feature tables and per-seat prices side by side, so the rival's price is always on the table. The question is whether your features are different enough for buyers to notice.

cards.title: Most shops do both at once.
body: Many retailers watch a short list of items that customers know the price of, such as milk, batteries or a famous-brand drill. They keep those close to rivals so the store feels fair.
On items people rarely compare, like own-brand goods, specialty parts or advice at the counter, they price more freely.
A restaurant can do the same: keep the coffee near the café next door and price the signature dishes on their own merits.

image.label: Store shelf with a few tagged comparison items
image.brief: 매장 선반 일러스트. 몇 개 품목(우유, 건전지, 드릴)에만 "Compare" 노란 태그가 붙어 있고 나머지 자체 상품에는 태그 없음. 실제 브랜드 표시 없음.

cards.title: A rival's price is not a rival's strategy.
body: You see their price, not their costs. The chain may buy drills for less than you, or it may be losing money on purpose to pull people in. Copying its price can mean copying a loss.
And if everyone only watches each other, nobody watches customers. Matching every cut can turn into a price war where all sides earn less.
Before you match, check that the new price still covers the costs that come with each sale.

cards.title: Now it's a software tool.
body: You sell project-management software to small design agencies. The best-known rival charges $10 per user per month.
Your tool does everything theirs does, plus built-in invoicing. Agencies in your interviews say invoicing saves them a separate subscription. How do you set your price?

options.text: Charge $10, the same as the rival
options.feedback: Safe in a feature-by-feature comparison, but you give away the invoicing for free. Buyers may even read the equal price as equal value.
You may win some price shoppers, but you earn less per user and signal you're the cheaper copy. The rival can cut too.

options.text: Start from $10 and add for invoicing, say $14, and show the comparison
options.feedback: The rival's price is your anchor, and the difference is what you charge for. You'll need to show the invoicing saving clearly, or buyers will only see the higher number.

cards.title: Let rivals set your price only where customers compare.
body: Match on what's identical and visible. Everywhere else, start from the rival's price and charge for the difference.
**Try it today:** list your five best sellers. Next to each, write whether a customer could find the exact same thing elsewhere. Those are the only prices a rival should decide.
